• **About FINA World Championships:**

 
 
• The FINA World Crowns or World Aquatics Championships are the World Championships for aquatics sports **swimming, diving, high diving, open water swimming, cultural swimming, and water polo.**
 
• They're run by **FINA**, and all swimming events are queried in a long course( 50- metre) pool.

questions.question: A FIBA sanctioned game of basketball typically consists of _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 quarters of 10 minutes each.**__

__
 
• The playing time for a FIBA game is** 40 minutes, and that is divided into four 10-minute quarters.**
 
• FIBA quarters and clock time are shorter than that of the NBA by a total of 8 minutes.
 
• **Two-minute breaks follow the first and third quarters**, and the second quarter is followed by a **15-minute halftime break.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **About FIBA:**

 
 
• The International Basketball Federation is an **association of public associations which governs the sport of basketball worldwide.**
 
• Firstly known as the Fédération Internationale de handbasket- ball amateur** (hence FIBA)**, in** 1989 **it dropped the word amateur from its name but retained the acronym.
 
• **FIBA defines the rules of basketball, specifies the outfit and installations needed, organizes transnational competitions, regulates the transfer of athletes across countries, and controls the appointment of transnational arbiters.**
 
• An aggregate of **213 public coalitions** are now members, organized since** 1989 into five zones Africa, Americas, Asia, Europe, and Oceania.**

questions.question: The term ‘Follow – On’ is used in which of the following games/sports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cricket.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term** ‘Follow – On’ **is used in** cricket.**
 
• A team who **batted second in **the sport of cricket but scored significantly **fewer runs** than the team that** bat first** can be obliged to** follow-on,** or to play their **second innings **right after their first.
 
• The **side that batted first** may impose the follow-on.
 
• By** speeding up the second innings** of the second team, it aims to lower the** likelihood of a drawn outcome.**
 
• Only in the** types of cricket **where each team often bats twice—most notably **domestic first-class cricket** and** international Test cricket—**does the follow-on occur.
 
• **Boundary, LBW, Beamer, Appeal, Bails, Dolly, Edge** etc. are other terms used in cricket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hockey:**

 
 
• **16-yard hit, Advancing, Back-line, Bully, Center pass , Clearing, Dangerous Play,** etc. are some of the terms used in the game of **hockey**. 
 
 
 
• **Badminton:**
 
 
• **The backcourt, Birdie, Carry, Center position, Cross-court, Drop shot, Flick, Forecourt**, etc. are some of the terms used in the game of **badminton**.
 
 
 
• **Football:**
 
 
• **Line of scrimmage, fumble, muff, huddle, blitz, sack, scramble, special teams, **etc. are some of the terms used in the game football.

questions.question: The first unified Asian Games were held in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The **First Asian Games** was the official name for the **1951 Asian Games.**
 
• From **March 4 to March 11, 1951, New Delhi, India**, hosted a multisport tournament.
 
• The Games received names like** First Asiad and 1951 Asiad.**
 
• A **total of 57 events **from eight sports and disciplines featured **489 athletes from 11 Asian National Olympic Committees**.
 
• The **Asian Games Federation** was originally founded in **Delhi on February 13th, 1949**.
 
• **Delhi** has been selected as the **inaugural Asian Games** host city by a unanimous vote.
 
• With** 24 gold medals** and **60 total medals **earned,** Japanese **competitors led the way.
 
• **51 total medals** were won by India, with **15 **of them being gold. 
 
• In a medal table, it came in **second place.**
 
• The** second** Asian Games were held in the year **1954 in Manila, Philippines.**
 
• From then onwards, the games were organized **once in four years.**

questions.question: The Durand Cup, Santosh Trophy and Rovers Cup are related to which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Football__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The Durand Cup

 
 
• The Durand Cup is the oldest football tournament in India.
 
• The Tournament was first held in 1888 in Annadale, Shimla. 
 
• It is co-hosted by the Durand Football Tournament Society (DFTS).
 
• The Tournament is the oldest existing football tournament in Asia.
 
 
 
• The Rovers Cup
 
 
• The Rovers Cup was an annual football tournament held in India.
 
• It was the second-oldest tournament in India.
 
• The championship was started by some British football enthusiasts in Bombay, Maharashtra in 1891, as a form of amusement.
 
• Rovers Cup was organized by Western India Football Association (WIFA).
 
• Rovers Cup was Founded in 1890.
 
 
 
• The Santosh Trophy
 
 
• It is an Indian football tournament in which the states of the country along with some government institutions participate.
 
• This is held annually since 1941.
 
• Bengal was the first winner of the competition held in 1941.
 
• The trophy is named after the late Maharaja Sir Manmatha Nath Roy Chowdhary of Santosh.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian football players is nicknamed as ‘Sikkimese Sniper’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhaichung Bhutia.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhaichung Bhutia is also known as the Sikkimese Sniper.

 
 
• He is a former Indian national footballer and is considered the epitome of the rise of Indian football.
 
• He was born on 15 December 1976 in Tinkitam, Sikkim, and played as a striker all his career.
 
• Bhutia is known for his powerful shots and his pinpoint accuracy in front of the goal.
 
• His hunger for goals and his passion for the game made him the father figure of Indian football.
 
• Bhaichung has also captained the national side and currently plays the role of manager at the Sikkim state football club.
 
• Bhutia has represented the following teams - **India, East Bengal, JCT Mills, Bury, Mohun Bagan, Perak FA, Selangor MK Land, and United Sikkim.**
 
• Bhaichung Bhutia made his club professional debut in 1993 for Calcutta-based East Bengal where he would make nine appearances, scoring 4 goals in the league.
 
• In 2008, He had refused to carry the Olympic torch to show support and solidarity for the people of Tibet and their struggle.
